display.purpose: The single largest text on a view. Empty-state headlines only, at most one per screen.

title.purpose: Buttons and menu items. The interactive ramp.

body.purpose: Field values, descriptions, list content. Cap prose at 65 to 75ch.

label.purpose: Tab titles, sidebar rows, field labels, inline status. The densest and most-used step.

caption.purpose: Step numbers, badges, branch tags, metadata. Below this, only glyphs.

mono.purpose: Commands, paths, branch names, run output, prompt marks. Never labels or headings.

shadows.name: menu-drop
shadows.purpose: Popover menus, the branch picker, context menus. One of only two shadows in the system.

shadows.name: dialog-drop
shadows.purpose: Modal dialogs. Deeper and wider because a dialog sits further from the panel.

shadows.name: node-lift
shadows.purpose: Canvas node. The documented exception to the Two-Shadow Rule: a node is lifted off a world plane, not layered in the chrome.

borders.name: hairline-seam
borders.purpose: Seam between adjacent layers of the ramp, such as sidebar against pane area.

borders.name: hairline-panel
borders.purpose: Edge of a floating surface: menus, dialogs, popovers.

borders.name: hairline-field
borders.purpose: Resting border of an input field.

borders.name: focus-field
borders.purpose: Focused input. The border alone shifts; no glow, no ring expansion.

surfaceWashes.name: hover-danger
surfaceWashes.purpose: Destructive control hover. Never a fill at rest.

surfaceWashes.name: field-recess
surfaceWashes.purpose: Input field background. Fields are recessed washes, not raised boxes.

glass.name: glass-chrome
glass.purpose: Toolbar and tab strip under native Liquid Glass.

glass.name: glass-panel
glass.purpose: Menus and dialogs under native Liquid Glass.

glass.name: glass-tab-active
glass.purpose: Active tab under native Liquid Glass.

motion.name: spin
motion.purpose: In-progress step indicator. Must degrade under prefers-reduced-motion to a static indicator that still reports the running state.

motion.name: pulse
motion.purpose: Attention or pending state, cycling opacity 1 to 0.35. Same reduced-motion obligation.

narrative.overview:
Farol is an aircraft panel, not a webpage. Every indicator earns its space, every reading is unambiguous, and the whole surface is legible under pressure at a glance. The instrument is dense because density is correct here: an operator who has to hunt for the state of a run has been failed by the panel. Small type, tight gaps, and exact alignment are the vocabulary. What makes it a control surface rather than clutter is that no element is present for decoration, and every value is deliberate.

The panel is dark, but not for atmosphere. It is dark because the thing it houses, a real terminal at #080D17, is the darkest surface in the app, and everything else steps up from it in near-black tints. Depth is built by stacking surfaces, not by painting shadows. The chrome around the terminal is a slightly lighter grey; the sidebar a shade between; a floating panel a shade above that. This is why the system reads as one machined object rather than a stack of cards.

Color is almost absent, and that absence is the design. The surface is a run of neutral greys, and the only saturated values in the entire system are signal: blue for what is selected or actionable, green for pass, red for fail, violet for an AI step, amber for a result that has gone stale. A screen where more than a sliver is colored is a screen where the signals have stopped meaning anything. This system explicitly rejects the neon hacker terminal, the AI-product gradient, the CI dashboard’s badge soup, and the generic Electron app that forgot which platform it was running on.
keyCharacteristics: Navy tonal layering from Deep Navy #080D17 through Dark Surface #111827 to Slate Panel #1F2937
One accent (#2563EB), four status colors, nothing else saturated
Dense native type ramp, 9px to 15px, weights 600 and 700 only
Small radii (3px to 8px), hairline rgba(255,255,255,0.12) borders
Flat at rest; shadows exist only under things that float
macOS system fonts and materials, never a substitute stack

rules.name: The Signal Rule
rules.body: Saturated color is a reading, never a finish. Blue, green, red, violet, and amber appear only where the interface is reporting state or offering the primary action. If a saturated color appears anywhere it is not reporting something, delete it. A typical screen is under 5% saturated pixels.

rules.name: The Pitch Floor Rule
rules.body: Terminal and run-log surfaces stay at #080D17, fully opaque, always. When the window is running native Liquid Glass and every other surface goes translucent, content panes do not. Contrast under the user’s own shell theme outranks the material effect.

rules.name: The Status Never Alone Rule
rules.body: Green, red, amber, and grey always travel with a glyph or a word. "Passed", "Failed", "Skipped", "Not run on feature/x". A user who cannot distinguish the hues must still read the panel correctly.

rules.name: The Weight-Not-Size Rule
rules.body: The ramp spans six points from top to bottom, so scale cannot carry hierarchy. Promote with weight (600) or with the text color ramp; never by inventing a size step outside the ladder.

rules.name: The Mono Means Code Rule
rules.body: SF Mono is reserved for text the machine will read or did emit: commands, paths, branch names, run output, prompt marks. Monospace on a label, a heading, or a button is decoration borrowed from the hacker-terminal aesthetic, and is prohibited.

rules.name: The Nine-Pixel Floor Rule
rules.body: Nothing below 9px, and 9px only for non-essential metadata that repeats elsewhere. Any text carrying meaning that appears nowhere else is 11px or larger.

rules.name: The Two-Shadow Rule
rules.body: The system has two shadows. Menus get Menu Drop, dialogs get Dialog Drop, and everything else gets none. A hover state that reaches for a shadow is a hover state that should have changed its background instead. The one exception is a canvas node (0 8px 24px rgba(0,0,0,0.35)), which is genuinely lifted off a world plane rather than layered in the chrome.

rules.name: The Ramp-Is-The-Z-Order Rule
rules.body: To raise a surface, move it up the neutral ramp; to recess one, move it down. Never simulate depth on an in-flow element with a shadow, an inner glow, or a gradient.

rules.name: The Glass Exception
rules.body: When native Liquid Glass is active, chrome surfaces become translucent tints of rgba(28,28,30,0.38–0.42) and panels rgba(44,44,46,0.72), but the layer ordering is unchanged and content panes stay opaque. Glass is a platform material the window receives, never an effect the interface applies for looks.

dos: Do build depth by moving surfaces along the neutral ramp (#080D17 → #1F2937), reinforced with hairline #273449 borders.
Do keep terminal and run-log panes fully opaque at #080D17, including when Liquid Glass is active.
Do use rgba(255,255,255,0.05–0.14) background washes for every hover state. That wash is the app’s hover language.
Do pair every status color with a glyph or word: "Passed", "Failed", "Skipped", "Not run on feature/x".
Do reserve SF Mono for commands, paths, branch names, and run output.
Do promote with weight (600) and the text color ramp, since the type ramp spans only 9px to 15px.
Do honor prefers-reduced-motion on bfspin and bfpulse, degrading to a static indicator that still reports the running state.
Do check dim metadata (#94A3B8, #64748B, #475569) for 4.5:1 against its actual surface, including the translucent glass variants where the effective background shifts.
Do show the real result, including git’s refusal message or a missing CLI on PATH, in the interface’s own type rather than swallowing it.
donts: Don’t build the generic Electron app. No browser-default buttons, no substitute font stack in place of SF Pro and SF Mono, no web-styled scrollbars over the app’s own 10px rgba(255,255,255,0.14) thumb. If it reads as a website in a frame, rewrite it.

Don’t build the CI dashboard. No heavy tables, no status-badge soup, no cluttered configuration forms. A pipeline is a node canvas to author and a numbered chain to read, never a grid of identical cards.
Don’t build the neon hacker terminal. No matrix green, no glow, no text-shadow, no cyberpunk styling, and no decorative monospace on labels, headings, or buttons.
Don’t build the AI-product gradient SaaS. No purple or blue gradients, no glassmorphism applied as decoration, no hero-metric cards, no sparkle icons. AI Violet marks a step type and nothing more.
Don’t use background-clip: text with a gradient anywhere. Emphasis is weight or color, never a gradient fill.
Don’t use border-left or border-right above 1px as a colored stripe on a row, step, or panel. Status goes in a glyph, a word, or the text color.
Don’t add a fourth shadow. Menus get 0 12px 32px rgba(0,0,0,0.5), dialogs get 0 18px 48px rgba(0,0,0,0.55), canvas nodes get 0 8px 24px rgba(0,0,0,0.35), everything else gets none.
Don’t reach for a modal. Splits, panes, inline editors, and the sidebar exist precisely so state can be shown in place.
Don’t apply blur or translucency by hand. Glass is a native material the window receives; content panes never take it.
Don’t restyle the inside of a terminal pane. The user’s prompt, theme, and colors pass through untouched.
Don’t show anything green that was not earned on the current branch. Stale results are Stale Amber and labeled with the branch they came from.
